info.description:
Public API for Stacked creators and agencies.

> **Beta.** The API is in beta. Documented behavior is stable for the
> operations listed here; any breaking change is announced to API key
> holders before it ships. Send questions, bug reports, and access
> requests to support@stacked.com. The API is meant to be called from
> servers: browser origins other than Stacked's own are not allowed by
> CORS.

## Quick start

1. Send your API key as `Authorization: Bearer stk_live_your_api_key`.
2. Call
   [`GET /external-service/v1/creators`](#tag/account/GET/external-service/v1/creators)
   and choose a `userId`.
3. Pass that id as `creatorUserId` on requests that act on a creator.

```bash
curl "https://api.stacked.com/external-service/v1/chats?creatorUserId=CREATOR_USER_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer stk_live_your_api_key"
```

## Authentication

Every API operation requires a bearer token — either your API key or an
OAuth access token from Connect Stacked, which authenticates identically:

```
Authorization: Bearer stk_live_your_api_key
```

Direct API-key access requires approval for the account. Once approved,
get the key from External API settings in your Stacked dashboard. Keys
begin with `stk_live_`. A missing, unrecognized, or revoked key is rejected
with 401.

The raw key is shown exactly once, when it is issued. Stacked stores only
a hash of it; later listings show the key prefix only. Lose the key and you
must replace it.

## Connect Stacked (OAuth 2.0)

An API key is a single secret that carries every permission your account
has and never expires. "Connect Stacked" is the alternative: an
application asks for the permissions it needs, a creator approves them,
and the application receives its own credentials — scoped to what was
approved, expiring hourly, and revocable by either side without
disturbing anything else.

The flow is OAuth 2.0 authorization code. **PKCE with `S256` is required
of every client**, confidential ones included.

### Registering an application

Registering an application requires API access approval for the registering
account. There are two kinds, and which one you are building decides how
you register it.

**An application only your own account will connect** — your script, your
bot, your agency's internal tool. Register it yourself from the Developer
page in your Stacked dashboard. It works immediately: nobody else can be
shown its consent screen, so there is nothing for Stacked to review. This
is the credential to reach for instead of putting an API key in your
code.

**An application other creators will connect** — a product. Submit it
from the same page and Stacked reviews it before any creator can connect
it, because approving it means vouching for it to people who did not
build it. Until it is approved the application is inert: its authorize
link resolves to nothing. Stacked may approve it for fewer scopes than
you asked for, and the consent screen tells the creator which of your
requested permissions were not granted. If you are not a Stacked creator
and have no dashboard, contact support@stacked.com instead.

Either way you receive a `client_id` immediately. **You generate the
`client_secret` yourself**, from the Developer page, once the application
is approved — it is displayed once and Stacked keeps only a digest, so
nobody at Stacked can read it back to you. The same button rotates it. A
public client (mobile, desktop, CLI, single-page app) simply never
generates one and authenticates with PKCE alone.

An application you register cannot request permissions the registering
account does not already hold: you cannot delegate access you do not
have.

### Who can connect

**Approved public applications** — applications other accounts can connect,
not just their registering account — can be connected by a creator to their
own creator account or an agency where they are an active owner. The
connecting account does not need direct API-key approval or an API key.
This public reach is separate from whether the OAuth client authenticates
with a secret or PKCE alone.

**Owner-scoped applications** can only be connected to their registering
account, which must still have approved API access. Approval is per account:
approval for a creator account does not approve an agency, or the reverse.
Request direct API access from the Developer page if that account needs it.

Stacked's signed-in consent UI reads `requiresApiAccess` from
`GET /external-service/v1/oauth/clients/{clientId}`. It is `true` only for
owner-scoped applications. The `apiAccessApproved` field from
`GET /external-service/v1/oauth/connectable-accounts` still reports the
account's actual direct API access approval; it blocks consent only when
`requiresApiAccess` is also `true`.

Public-app scopes are limited to the permissions requested, approved for the
application, and granted by the account through consent — not by the
connecting account's API keys. Owner-scoped grants are additionally limited
to the account's current API-key scopes, including at code exchange and
refresh. Always read the token response's `scope` field rather than assuming
every requested permission was granted.

1. Send the creator to the consent page:

   ```
   https://stacked.com/oauth/authorize
     ?client_id=stk_ci_...
     &redirect_uri=https://yourapp.example.com/callback
     &response_type=code
     &scope=chat:read%20chat:write
     &state=RANDOM
     &code_challenge=BASE64URL(SHA256(verifier))
     &code_challenge_method=S256
   ```

   `redirect_uri` must exactly match one you registered. A creator who
   declines is sent back with `?error=access_denied`.

2. Exchange the returned `code` for tokens:

   ```bash
   curl -X POST "https://api.stacked.com/external-service/v1/oauth/token" \
     -u "stk_ci_your_client_id:stk_cs_your_client_secret" \
     -d grant_type=authorization_code \
     -d code=stk_ac_... \
     -d redirect_uri=https://yourapp.example.com/callback \
     -d code_verifier=YOUR_VERIFIER
   ```

   A public client (mobile or single-page app) has no secret and sends
   `client_id` in the body instead; PKCE is what authenticates it.

3. Call the API with the access token exactly as you would with an API
   key: `Authorization: Bearer stk_at_...`. Access tokens last one hour;
   an expired one is rejected with 401 and the message
   `access token expired`. Get a new one with the refresh token:

   ```bash
   curl -X POST "https://api.stacked.com/external-service/v1/oauth/token" \
     -u "stk_ci_your_client_id:stk_cs_your_client_secret" \
     -d grant_type=refresh_token -d refresh_token=stk_rt_...
   ```

Access tokens carry the account and scopes the creator approved, so
[`GET /external-service/v1/me`](#tag/account/GET/external-service/v1/me) and
[`GET /external-service/v1/creators`](#tag/account/GET/external-service/v1/creators)
work the same as for a key. Creators can disconnect your app at any time
from their Stacked dashboard, which immediately invalidates its tokens;
`POST /external-service/v1/oauth/revoke` (RFC 7009) lets you do the same
from your side — a client may only revoke its own tokens. Which token you
send matters: revoking the **refresh token** ends the whole grant, exactly
as a creator disconnecting would, while revoking an **access token**
retires only that token and leaves the grant live, so you can immediately
mint another. Rotating a direct API key does not disconnect apps, and changing
its scopes does not narrow public-app grants. Disconnecting an app, revoking
the application, or staff explicitly revoking the account's API access
still revokes the affected grants and tokens.

Server metadata is published at
`GET /external-service/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`.

Stacked stores only a digest of your authorization codes, access tokens,
refresh tokens and client secret — never the values themselves — so
nobody at Stacked can read or replay them. A client secret is shown
exactly once, at generation. A refresh token is issued once and then
echoed back unchanged on every refresh (Stacked does not rotate refresh
tokens), so store the value you were given. If you lose a refresh token,
send the creator back through consent; if you lose the client secret,
generate a new one.

**A refresh token lasts 90 days from its last use.** Every successful
refresh slides that window forward, so an app in regular use never has to
re-prompt; one that goes 90 days without refreshing gets
`400 invalid_grant` and must send the creator through consent again.

Two things to know about the tokens themselves:

- **A grant has one live access token.** Refreshing supersedes the
  previous one rather than running two side by side, so refresh from one
  place in your application and retry a 401 rather than refreshing per
  worker.
- **Your identity is stable across refreshes.** Resources you own —
  webhook subscriptions in particular — stay yours when you refresh, and
  stay yours until the creator disconnects you.

Public clients (mobile, desktop, CLI) are supported and authenticate with
PKCE alone. A browser single-page app cannot call the token endpoint
directly today: its origin must be allowlisted first, so contact
support@stacked.com. Exchanging the code from your own server avoids this
entirely and is the better shape regardless.

## Creator and agency keys

Every API key acts as one account, reported by
[`GET /external-service/v1/me`](#tag/account/GET/external-service/v1/me)
as `account.type` and `account.id`:

- A **creator** key belongs to a creator account and can act only on that
  creator.
- An **agency** key belongs to the agency — not to the team member who
  created it — and can act on every creator currently connected to the
  agency through an accepted agency link. When a link is no longer accepted
  (the creator leaves, the agency ends the relationship, or the link is
  revoked) the key loses access to that creator immediately. The key keeps
  working if the person who created it leaves the agency; only an active
  agency owner can create, replace, or revoke agency keys.

When requesting API access from the dashboard, choose the creator account
or the agency the key is for (`accountType` and `accountId`). A user who
runs both a creator account and an agency requests and manages each
independently; replacing one never revokes the other.

## Choosing a creator

Most operations act on one creator. Pass the creator's `userId` as either
the `creatorUserId` query parameter or the `X-Stacked-Creator-User-Id`
header. When both are present, the query parameter wins.

You can only name a creator your API key has access to (see
[Creator and agency keys](#description/creator-and-agency-keys)). Naming
any other creator is rejected with 403. Call
[`GET /external-service/v1/creators`](#tag/account/GET/external-service/v1/creators)
to list the ones you can reach.

Only [`GET /external-service/v1/me`](#tag/account/GET/external-service/v1/me) and
[`GET /external-service/v1/creators`](#tag/account/GET/external-service/v1/creators)
do not take a creator id.

The [webhook destination](#tag/webhooks) operations are the one place where
an agency key may leave the creator out: it then manages the agency's own
destination, which receives the events of every creator linked to it. See
[Webhook setup and delivery](#description/webhook-setup-and-delivery).

## People in the API

- A **user** is a Stacked identity, always referenced by `userId`.
- A **member** is a user who holds (or held) a membership subscription with
  the creator. The `members` operations return one entry per user based on
  their latest subscription.
- A **membership subscription** is the billing and access relationship; a
  user can have several over time. `GET /members/{userId}/subscriptions`
  returns a member's full history.
- A **subscriber** is a member whose subscription is currently active
  (`status=active` or `status=expiring` on the members filter).
- A **follower** is a user connected to the creator through the follow
  feature; following does not require a subscription.
- A **member list** is a creator-defined group of members and followers,
  usable as a mass message audience.
- A **membership tier** is a recurring membership offering; a **membership
  promotion** is a temporary first-month discount applied to one or more
  tiers.
- A **tracking link** is a creator-owned attribution link; signups and
  purchases made through it are reported by its analytics.
- A **paid link** is a durable public page where anyone can buy a set of
  pay-per-view (PPV) content from the creator.

## Identifiers

Every id is an opaque string. Public ids (`postPublicId`, `listId`,
`massMessageId`, `subscriptionId`, `transactionId`, `promotionId`,
`trackingLinkId`, `paidLinkId`, webhook `id`) may
contain any characters, including `:`; store them whole and never split
them. How resources connect:

- `Member.subscriptionId` identifies the member's latest subscription;
  `GET /members/{userId}/subscriptions` returns that member's full history.
- `tier.stripeProductId` (from `GET /membership-tiers`, members, and
  subscriptions) is the tier id accepted by `tierStripeProductIds` on posts
  and by `recipients.tierStripeProductIds` on mass messages.
- `listId` from `GET /member-lists` is accepted by
  `recipients.memberListIds` on mass messages, alongside the system lists
  `system:all-members` and `system:following-only`.
- `assetPublicId` from the library is accepted by posts and mass messages.
- `TrackingLink.code` appears as `trackingLinkCode` on transactions made
  through that link.

## Pagination

Database-backed lists (posts, members, member subscriptions, member lists,
mass messages) are offset-paginated: pass `limit` and `offset`,
and continue while the response includes `nextOffset` (pass it back as
`offset`). Offset pages are not stable if items are inserted while you
page. Chats, followers, transactions, paid links, and mass-message recipient
outcomes are cursor-paginated: pass the
returned `nextCursor` as `cursor` and continue while it is present. A page
may contain fewer than `limit` items even when another page exists.

## Money and time

Amounts are integers in the minor unit of the accompanying `currency`
(cents for USD), and `currency` is a lowercase ISO 4217 code. Three amount
families appear:

- **Paid** (`paidUnitAmount`, `Member.totalSpend`, webhook
  `paidUnitAmount`): what the buyer paid, including buyer-side fees,
  before refunds.
- **Gross** (`saleUnitAmount`, earnings `grossUnitAmount`): the creator's
  realized sale, excluding buyer processing fees and tax, before platform,
  agency, and affiliate fees, after refunds.
- **Net** (`netCreatorUnitAmount`, earnings `netUnitAmount`): creator
  take-home after those fees, after refunds.

Timestamps on members, subscriptions, posts, member lists, mass messages,
insights, and webhook envelopes are RFC3339 in UTC, and analytics buckets
are UTC calendar days. The chat operations keep their original numeric
forms: chat message times are epoch milliseconds and chat, tip-request,
and reaction times are epoch seconds, as noted on each field.

## Asynchronous operations

Posts accepted by `createPost` publish once every attachment is ready,
without an open client connection. Until then, unscheduled posts remain
`processing`. Scheduled posts also wait for `scheduledAt`; background
queue backlog can delay publication after both conditions are met.
For compatibility, post reads also return unfinished drafts from the
Fanfix app as `processing`. Those drafts require submission in the app;
`processing` alone does not guarantee automatic publication.
Mass messages move `scheduled` → `queued` → `sending` → `completed` or
`failed`, and can be `canceled` while scheduled. Poll the resource, or
subscribe to matching webhook events, which arrive within about a minute
of the change.

## Retries

Reads, 429s, and 502s are safe to retry (after `Retry-After` for 429).
Retry creates only with an `Idempotency-Key`, and retry other writes only
after confirming the state with a read. Member list and mass message
mutations are idempotent by design (adding an existing member or canceling
an already canceled message is a no-op, as is deleting an already
deactivated membership tier or tracking link, or stopping an already
stopped promotion). To change a scheduled mass message, cancel it and
create a new one; to change a membership promotion or a tracking link,
stop or delete it and create a replacement.

## Aggregating across creators

`GET /earnings` and `GET /subscribers/summary` accept a comma-separated
`creatorUserIds` query parameter (at most 10) instead of a single creator. Every creator must be
accessible to the API key, otherwise the whole request is rejected with
403. Each row in the response carries its `creatorUserId`; rows are not
summed across creators because currencies may differ.

Each operation lists its required API-key scope. The available scopes are:

| Scope | Allows |
| --- | --- |
| `chat:read` | Read chats and messages |
| `chat:write` | Create chats; send text and tip requests; edit and delete messages |
| `media:send` | Manage library assets; send media and AI voice messages |
| `ppv:send` | Send pay-per-view messages and pay-per-view mass messages; manage paid links |
| `posts:read` | List and inspect posts |
| `posts:write` | Create, update, reschedule, and delete posts |
| `members:read` | List and inspect members, their subscriptions, membership tiers and promotions, followers, and member lists |
| `members:write` | Create, update, and delete membership tiers; create and stop membership promotions; create and manage member lists |
| `mass_messages:read` | List and inspect mass messages and recipient outcomes |
| `mass_messages:write` | Preview audiences, create and cancel mass messages (`ppv:send` is also required for pay-per-view mass messages) |
| `insights:read` | Earnings, subscriber growth, the transaction ledger, and tracking link analytics |
| `tracking_links:manage` | List, create, and delete tracking links |
| `webhooks:manage` | List, create, and delete webhook destinations |

Account metadata and creator listing do not require a scope, but they
still require authentication. A key without the required
scope is rejected with 403.

## Errors

Every error responds with the same envelope, whatever the status code:

```json
{"error": "message"}
```

Error messages are human-readable and may change. Use the HTTP status code,
not the message text, for program logic.

The two OAuth endpoints are the exception, because RFC 6749 defines their
shape: `POST /external-service/v1/oauth/token` and
`POST /external-service/v1/oauth/revoke` respond with
`{"error": "invalid_grant", "error_description": "..."}`, where `error` is
a machine-readable code (`invalid_request`, `invalid_client`,
`invalid_grant`, `unsupported_grant_type`, `slow_down`, `server_error`)
that you *should* branch on, and `error_description` is the prose.

Every operation response includes an `X-Request-Id` header. Supply your own value to
correlate a request across systems, or omit it and the API generates one.

## Limits

Request bodies are limited to 16 MiB. A larger body is rejected with 413.

## Rate limits

Authenticated requests are counted in fixed one-minute windows per API
key (requests rejected with 400, 401, or 403 before reaching an operation
are not counted). Every key may make 600 requests per minute across all
operations. Stricter windows apply on top of that:

- **Writes, 120 per minute:** `POST/PATCH/DELETE` on posts, membership
  tiers, membership promotions, tracking links, paid links, member lists
  and their members, webhook destinations, and canceling mass messages.
- **Expensive reads, 60 per minute:** `GET /earnings`,
  `GET /subscribers/summary`, tracking link analytics, and mass-message
  recipient outcomes.
- **Mass message creation, 10 per minute per API key and creator.**
- **Mass message previews, 10 per minute per API key and creator,**
  counted separately from creation.

The OAuth endpoints are counted separately, since they are called before
there is a key to count against: `POST /external-service/v1/oauth/token`
and `POST /external-service/v1/oauth/revoke` allow **60 requests per minute
per client**, and
requests that fail client authentication are counted against the caller's
source address instead of the client. Exhausting either window returns
`429` with `{"error": "slow_down"}` and a `Retry-After` header.

Every counted response — success or error — carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`,
`X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix seconds when the
tightest applicable window resets); they are not repeated on each
operation below. If the counter is temporarily unavailable the request is
allowed and the headers are omitted. When a window is exhausted the
request is rejected with 429 and a `Retry-After` header in seconds; wait
that long and retry. Rejected (429) requests still count toward the
window. Limits are enforced across all API servers.

## Idempotent creates

Resource creates that document an `Idempotency-Key` header require it
(posts, member lists, mass messages, membership tiers and promotions,
tracking links, paid links); chat sends use the `sendIdempotencyKey` body
field instead. Creating a chat or a webhook destination is naturally
idempotent (one distinct chat per member set, one destination per key and
creator) and takes no key. The server stores the successful outcome of
the first keyed request for 24 hours, keyed by API key, creator,
operation, and the header value (1 to 128 bytes; longer keys are rejected
with 400). Retrying with the same key and the byte-identical body replays
the original status and body with an `Idempotent-Replayed: true` header.
Reusing the key with a different body (including reordered fields or
whitespace changes) is rejected with 409, as is a retry that overlaps an
in-flight request. Error responses are not stored: after a 4xx, correct
the request and retry with the same key; after a 5xx, retry as is.

## Webhook setup and delivery

The **[Webhook destinations](#tag/webhooks)** operations configure where
events are sent. The **Webhook events** reference describes the requests
Stacked sends to those destinations.

Create a destination with
[`POST /external-service/v1/webhooks`](#tag/webhooks/POST/external-service/v1/webhooks).
Save its signing secret immediately because it is shown only once. Stacked
then
sends the selected events to that HTTPS URL through Svix. Every event body
has the same envelope — `id`, `type`, `createdAt`, and `data` — and
`data.creatorUserId` names the creator the event belongs to. Payment
events carry `data.type` (membership, post, tip, ppv_message, …) so one
subscription covers every purchase kind, and `data.paidLinkId` when the
purchase came through a paid link. Event ids are
deterministic (`type:resourceId`, plus a qualifier for events that can
recur for one resource, such as `post.updated`, `subscription.renewed`, and
`payment.refunded`), so the same id is retained across retries, and the
same event is never delivered with two different ids. Treat ids as opaque strings. Chat events
are emitted as they happen. `asset.ready` is recorded atomically when the
upload producer makes an asset usable; it is not a historical library replay.
Post, follower, subscription, payment, and mass message events are derived
from Stacked's records within about a minute of the change, so a burst of
changes to one resource may collapse into fewer events.
Deliveries that fail are retried with exponential backoff (up to hourly)
for seven days.

Verify `svix-id`, `svix-timestamp`, and `svix-signature` with a Svix or
Standard Webhooks library and the exact, unmodified request bytes. Do not
parse and re-serialize the JSON before verification. Reject invalid or
stale signatures.

Deliveries are at least once and may arrive out of order. Store the body
`id` in a unique column, finish durable processing, and only then return a
2xx response. The same `id` is retained across delivery retries. Return a
non-2xx response when processing should be retried.

Example using the JavaScript `svix` package:

```js
import { Webhook } from "svix";

const rawBody = await request.text();
const event = new Webhook(process.env.STACKED_WEBHOOK_SECRET).verify(
  rawBody,
  {
    "svix-id": request.headers.get("svix-id"),
    "svix-timestamp": request.headers.get("svix-timestamp"),
    "svix-signature": request.headers.get("svix-signature"),
  },
);
```

A creator can have at most three destinations. A single API key can own
one destination for a creator. Subscriptions are immutable: delete and
recreate one to change its URL or event filters.

### One destination for a whole agency

An agency key that omits `creatorUserId` when creating a destination gets
an **agency-wide** destination: one URL, one signing secret, and one
delivery history for every creator currently linked to the agency. Tell the
creators apart by `data.creatorUserId`, which every envelope carries.

One event can belong to two of the agency's creators — a chat between them,
say — and arrives once for each. Both copies carry their own `id`, so
storing `id` in a unique column deduplicates redeliveries here exactly as
it does for a per-creator destination. The ids an agency-wide destination
receives are its own: do not expect them to match the ids the same event
carries at a per-creator destination.

Coverage follows the agency's links as they change. A creator who accepts a
link starts delivering to it with no call from you, and a creator who
leaves stops delivering — the destination, and its secret, are untouched
either way. Nothing is delivered for a creator whose link is not accepted,
who is banned, or who has deactivated their account.

An agency can have at most three agency-wide destinations, one per API key,
and they are counted against the agency rather than against any creator's
three. `GET` and `DELETE` follow the same rule as `POST`: with no
`creatorUserId` they address the agency's own destinations, and with one
they address that creator's. An agency key can hold both kinds at once; a
creator whose agency subscribes to the same events as one of your
per-creator destinations will deliver an event to each.

One destination is one endpoint, so the summed traffic of every linked
creator arrives at a single URL: subscribe only to the events you handle,
and return 2xx quickly.

  [Webhook setup and delivery](#description/webhook-setup-and-delivery).

### 2026-09-03

- **[`GET /external-service/v1/transactions`](#tag/insights/GET/external-service/v1/transactions)
  reports `paidLinkId`.** A `ppv_message` purchase made through a paid
  link now names that link on the transaction itself, matching
  `data.paidLinkId` on the corresponding
  `payment.*` webhook event. A missed or lost webhook delivery can
  therefore be reconciled from the ledger alone.
- **Connect Stacked (OAuth 2.0).** An application can act on a creator's
  behalf through the authorization code + PKCE flow instead of asking them
  for a manually issued API key. Access tokens authenticate exactly like a
  key. See
  [Connect Stacked (OAuth 2.0)](#description/connect-stacked-oauth-20)
  above.
- **OAuth token scopes were capped by the granting account's own API
  access.** Since 2026-09-08 this restriction applies only to owner-scoped
  applications. Narrowing that account's scopes narrows its owner-scoped
  tokens at their next refresh. A grant can come back with fewer scopes
  than the application asked for — read the `scope` field of the token
  response rather than assuming the request was met in full.
- **Banned and deactivated creators are no longer reachable.** An operation
  naming one answers `403`, the creator stops appearing in
  [`GET /external-service/v1/creators`](#tag/account/GET/external-service/v1/creators),
  and webhook destinations for that creator are removed. This applies to
  API keys and OAuth tokens alike. If
  the ban is lifted, API access resumes on its own; webhook destinations
  have to be created again.
- **The OAuth endpoints report their rate limit.**
  `POST /external-service/v1/oauth/token` and
  `POST /external-service/v1/oauth/revoke` return `X-RateLimit-Limit`,
  `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset`. Their window — 60
  requests per minute per client — is documented under
  [Rate limits](#description/rate-limits), along with the refresh token's
  90-day sliding lifetime under
  [Connect Stacked](#description/connect-stacked-oauth-20).
- **Paid-link price validation and state conflicts are explicit.** Create
  and update requests accept `unitAmount` values from 100 through
  100,000,000 minor units. A paid-link update returns `409 Conflict` when
  its payment provider or current account configuration cannot support the
  requested price change.

### 2026-09-01

- **A paid link can be edited after it is created.**
  [`PATCH /external-service/v1/paid-links/{paidLinkId}`](#tag/paid-links/PATCH/external-service/v1/paid-links/{paidLinkId})
  accepts `unitAmount`, which prices future checkouts; `assetPublicIds`,
  the assets the link sells, in display order; `caption`; and
  `customThumbnailAssetPublicId`, the locked preview image. An empty string
  clears the caption or the preview image. Existing purchases and their
  attribution are unaffected by a repricing.

### 2026-08-29

- **The Stacked API opens in beta.** Creators and agencies can request API
  access from the Developer page in the Stacked dashboard and call the
  operations documented here: account and creator listing, members,
  subscriptions and followers, member lists, posts, chats and messaging,
  mass messages, the media library, membership tiers and promotions, paid
  links, tracking links, insights, and webhooks. An agency key acts on
  every creator currently linked to the agency; a creator key acts on its
  own creator.

post.description:
Registers up to 20 new library assets and returns upload targets: presigned S3 multipart upload URLs for image/audio files and thumbnails, and Bunny TUS upload data for videos. Each response entry corresponds to the request file at the same array index.
Images and videos receive a generated thumbnail and blurhash when no thumbnail is supplied. To override that preview, supply both an image `thumbnailMimeType` and positive `thumbnailFileSize`, then upload and complete the returned `thumbnailUpload`. Audio has no automatic preview. Generated previews are exposed through `thumbnailUrl`, `thumbnailMimeType`, `thumbnailWidth`, `thumbnailHeight`, and `blurhash` once ready.
For each `fileUpload` or `thumbnailUpload`, split the file into `partSize` byte chunks. PUT each chunk to the URL at the same array position using `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, and save the response `ETag`. After every part succeeds, call `completeLibraryAssetUploads` with the returned `bucket`, `key`, and `uploadId`, plus the ETags in URL order.
For each `bunnyUpload`, use a TUS client with endpoint `https://video.bunnycdn.com/tusupload`. Send `tusSignature`, `uploadExpiration`, `videoId`, and `libraryId` as the `AuthorizationSignature`, `AuthorizationExpire`, `VideoId`, and `LibraryId` headers. Send the file MIME type and a non-empty filename as the TUS `filetype` and `title` metadata values. Bunny uploads do not use the completion endpoint.
Audio uses the same multipart completion flow as images, with optional durationSec (finite and non-negative) and no image dimensions. Uploaded audio is asynchronously normalized to AAC/M4A by upload-service. Inspect the returned assetPublicId with getLibraryAsset or subscribe to asset.ready before using it in a message, campaign, or post. Ready means usable by those operations, not that every derived metadata field is final.
Side effect: creates pending asset records and S3/Bunny upload sessions. Unknown request fields are rejected. Requires the `media:send` scope.

Finalizes one or more S3 multipart uploads started via `createLibraryAssetUploads`. Pass the `bucket`, `key` and `uploadId` from the upload target and the ETag returned by S3 for each uploaded part, in the same order as the presigned URLs. Do not include Bunny TUS uploads. Unknown request fields are rejected. A 204 confirms multipart receipt; normalization and preview generation run asynchronously. Poll `getLibraryAsset` or await `asset.ready` before using the asset. Empty ETags are rejected, never removed or renumbered. Requires the `media:send` scope.

post.description:
Sends one direct message to every resolved recipient, immediately or at `scheduledAt` (up to 90 days ahead). Recipients are the union of `userIds` (each must be an active subscriber or follower), members of the given membership tiers, and members of the given member lists (custom lists or the system lists `system:all-members` and `system:following-only`), minus `excludeUserIds` and `excludeMemberListIds`. A request that resolves to no recipients, or to more than 1000, is rejected with 400. Provide `text`, `assetPublicIds`, `audioAssetPublicId`, and/or `ppv`. All assets must be the creator's fully processed library assets. A `ppv` block sends a pay-per-view message priced in minor units (minimum 100) and also requires the `ppv:send` scope.
Delivery is asynchronous: the response is the mass message resource with its `state`; poll `GET /mass-messages/{massMessageId}` for counts. An immediate send that cannot be queued returns the rejection status (400 for recipient or content problems, 502 for a dependency failure) and the resource is kept in the `failed` state. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe. Identical content to the same recipients within ten minutes is not sent twice: the new resource is linked to the earlier send and reports its counts. Preview selectors with `POST /mass-messages/preview` before creating a send. The preview is not a guarantee or reserved snapshot: recipients are resolved again on submission, including when a scheduled send is due. Blocked and inactive recipients are excluded. Before delivery, each queued recipient must still be a current subscriber or follower of the sending creator and must not be blocked in either direction. Ineligible recipients fail without sending; other recipients continue normally. Requires the `mass_messages:write` scope.

post.description: Resolves the same recipient selectors, ownership checks, and audience policy as creating a mass message, without creating a campaign, job, queue item, or message. Uses the existing `recipients` shape; no content or Idempotency-Key is required. At least one inclusion selector is required. `selectedCount` counts the unique selector union before exclusions; `excludedCount` counts unique selected users removed by explicit exclusions or because they are blocked, inactive, or outside the creator's current subscribers and followers. Overlaps count once; users outside the selection are not counted. `recipientCount = selectedCount - excludedCount`. Empty or over-1000 resolved audiences return 200 with `canSend: false`. Selector caps still apply: 1000 explicit inclusion/exclusion users and 50 IDs per tier/list selector. `canSend` checks audience size only, not message content, assets, PPV permission, or future delivery. `asOf` is the resolution start time, not a transactionally frozen snapshot. Membership and policy can change during or after resolution. No audience is reserved: immediate and scheduled sends resolve again when submitted. Limited to 10 previews/minute per key and creator in a separate budget from creates. Requires `mass_messages:write`.

Follow `nextCursor` until absent to traverse every result; there is no 500-recipient truncation. An optional `status` filters send progress, not reversion progress. Results are live, not a snapshot: a changing status can move a row into or out of a filter. `sent` means the send was recorded as successful, never that it was read. Failed sends can still expose IDs for messages sent before the failure. Reversion is reported separately from the latest recorded revert job; a failed revert can have deleted some messages and is not full success. Scheduled, canceled-before-submission, and failed-submission campaigns with no job return an empty page and their campaign `state`; an empty page does not imply successful delivery. An owned job with zero recipients likewise returns an empty page. A missing or inaccessible linked job returns 404 rather than another creator's data. `asOf` is the page-read start time, not a frozen snapshot. Limited to the 60/minute expensive-read budget. Requires `mass_messages:read`.

post.description: Creates a tracking link with a generated `code`. `destinationUrl` must be a Stacked page: a path such as `/@creator`, or an `https` URL on `stacked.com` or one of its subdomains; other hosts and plain `http` are rejected. Omit it to send visitors to the creator's membership page. Links cannot be edited: to change the name or destination, delete the link and create a new one (the new link gets a new `code`). The `Idempotency-Key` header is required (see [Idempotent creates](#description/idempotent-creates)). Requires the `tracking_links:manage` scope.

Idempotent-Replayed.description: Present with value `true` when this is a stored replay of an earlier request.

delete.description: Retires a tracking link: its `url` stops redirecting and attributing visitors, while its analytics history and the `trackingLinkCode` on past transactions are kept. The link remains visible with `isActive: false` through `includeInactive=true`. Deleting an already deleted link is a no-op. Requires the `tracking_links:manage` scope.

get.description: Returns the link's traffic and attribution totals for the window, with a daily UTC series. Attribution rules: a click sets a 30-day visitor cookie and the most recent link wins; a signup is attributed once per user, to the link they arrived through; a purchase is attributed when the buyer clicked the link within the previous three hours (or reached checkout through it). `subscriptions` counts distinct attributed buyers and `purchases` counts attributed payments. `netUnitAmount` is the creator's take-home from attributed purchases in minor units of `currency`, after refunds. Window parameters follow the insights operations (default the last 30 days, at most 366 days). Requires the `insights:read` scope.

Lists the creator's purchase ledger for the window `[startTime, endTime)` (defaults to the last 30 days), newest first, cursor-paginated: pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor`. `limit` defaults to 50 and is capped at 250. Succeeded and refunded purchases are included; set `includeFailed=true` to also include failed payment attempts. Filter by `type` or `buyerUserId`. Requires the `insights:read` scope.

post.description:
Creates one destination for this API key and creator. An API key can
own one destination per creator, and a creator can have at most three
destinations across all API keys. Destinations cannot be edited; to
change the URL or events, delete and recreate the destination.

An agency key that omits `creatorUserId` creates an **agency-wide**
destination instead: one URL and one signing secret for the events of
every creator currently linked to the agency, told apart by
`data.creatorUserId`. Coverage follows the agency's links as creators
join and leave, with no further calls. An agency can own three of
these, one per API key, counted against the agency rather than against
any creator's three. A creator key must always name its creator. See
[Webhook setup and delivery](#description/webhook-setup-and-delivery).

The signing secret is returned only in this response. Svix sends JSON
POST requests with `svix-id`, `svix-timestamp`, and `svix-signature`
headers (or the equivalent unbranded `webhook-*` headers). Use a Svix
verification library with the raw request body; it checks the signature
and timestamp tolerance. Do not verify parsed and re-serialized JSON.

Delivery is at least once. The body `id` is stable across retries, so
store processed ids and return a 2xx response only after durable
processing. Svix retries failures and may disable repeatedly failing
destinations. Requires the `webhooks:manage` scope.

`creatorUserId` the destination was created with; an agency key deleting
an agency-wide destination omits it. Requires the `webhooks:manage`
scope.
